title: Semi-free dg modules are homotopically projective
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain the module categories below. A small dg category $\mathcal B$ over $\mathbf Z$ has a set of objects and cochain complexes $\mathcal B(U,V)$, with unital associative chain-map compositions. A cochain complex has differential of degree $1$ with square zero. A right dg module $M$ has complexes $M(U)$ and unital associative chain-map actions $M(V)\otimes\mathcal B(U,V)\to M(U)$. Its cohomology is $H^r(M(U))=\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$; acyclic means these groups vanish for every $U,r$, and an objectwise quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all these groups. The representable module $\mathcal B(-,U)$ has action given by composition. The shift $M[n]$ has $M[n]^r=M^{r+n}$, differential $(-1)^n d_M$, and the unchanged right graded action. A graded module map of degree $r$ satisfies $f(ma)=f(m)a$; the complex of such maps is $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(M,N)$, with differential $df=d_Nf-(-1)^rfd_M$. A module $P$ is homotopically projective if this complex is acyclic for every objectwise acyclic $N$. A semi-free module $P$ has a filtration by dg submodules $0=P_0\subset P_1\subset\cdots$, with $P=\bigcup_{i\geq0}P_i$, each inclusion split as a graded module map, and each quotient $P_{i+1}/P_i$ isomorphic as a dg module to a coproduct of shifts of representables.

Every semi-free right dg $\mathcal B$-module is homotopically projective.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 14.8 (right modules by passage to the opposite dg category), printed pp. 36-37; compare the dg-algebra case in Stacks tag 09KM, label dga-lemma-property-P-K-projective, literature/stacks-project/dga.tex. Section 14.8 explicitly states the dg-category version.

proof.text: Let $N$ be objectwise acyclic, let $r\in\mathbf Z$, and let $f$ be a degree-$r$ cocycle in $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(P,N)$. Thus $d_Nf=(-1)^rfd_P$. By the displayed definition of the Hom differential it suffices to construct a graded module map $h$ of degree $r-1$ with $d_Nh+(-1)^rhd_P=f$.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: Choose the filtration in the statement. Write $Q_i=P_{i+1}/P_i\simeq\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I_i}\mathcal B(-,U_\alpha)[n_\alpha]$. A graded retraction $\rho_i:P_{i+1}\to P_i$ yields a graded section of the quotient: $s_i(\bar x)=x-j_i\rho_i(x)$, independent of the lift $x$, since $\rho_i j_i=1$. Hence $P_{i+1}=P_i\oplus s_i(Q_i)$ as graded modules.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: The identity $1_{U_\alpha}$ in the $\alpha$th shifted representable is a closed element of degree $k_\alpha=-n_\alpha$; let $e_\alpha=s_i(1_{U_\alpha})$. Since the quotient map is a chain map, $d_Pe_\alpha\in P_i$. At each object every element of $s_i(Q_i)$ is a finite sum of terms $e_\alpha a_\alpha$: indeed each element $a\in\mathcal B(V,U_\alpha)$ equals $1_{U_\alpha}a$. Thus specifying images of the $e_\alpha$ of the required degrees specifies a unique graded module map on this summand, by the formula $e_\alpha a\mapsto y_\alpha a$ and additivity.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: Start with $h_0=0$ on $P_0=0$. Suppose $h_i:P_i\to N$ has degree $r-1$ and satisfies $d_Nh_i+(-1)^rh_id_P=f|_{P_i}$. For a cell $e=e_\alpha$ of degree $k=k_\alpha$ put $z_e=f(e)-(-1)^rh_i(d_Pe)\in N(U_\alpha)^{k+r}$. Since $d_P^2e=0$, the induction equation at $d_Pe$ gives $d_Nh_i(d_Pe)=f(d_Pe)$. Consequently $d_Nz_e=(-1)^rf(d_Pe)-(-1)^rf(d_Pe)=0$.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: Acyclicity of $N(U_\alpha)$ says precisely that every cycle in degree $k+r$ is a boundary. Choose $y_e\in N(U_\alpha)^{k+r-1}$ with $d_Ny_e=z_e$, for all cells of this layer. These choices range over a set in the fixed enlarged universes. Define $h_{i+1}|_{P_i}=h_i$ and $h_{i+1}(e_\alpha a)=y_{e_\alpha}a$. The graded direct-sum decomposition makes this well-defined and additive; associativity of the actions makes it module-linear, and $|y_e|=|e|+r-1$ gives its degree.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: Check the required equation on homogeneous $ea$ as well as on $P_i$. The chain-map action gives $d_P(ea)=(d_Pe)a+(-1)^k e(d_{\mathcal B}a)$ and $d_N(y_ea)=(d_Ny_e)a+(-1)^{k+r-1}y_e(d_{\mathcal B}a)$. Therefore $(d_Nh_{i+1}+(-1)^rh_{i+1}d_P)(ea)=(d_Ny_e+(-1)^rh_i(d_Pe))a+\bigl((-1)^{k+r-1}+(-1)^{k+r}\bigr)y_e(d_{\mathcal B}a)=f(e)a=f(ea)$. On $P_i$ this is the induction hypothesis; additivity proves it on $P_{i+1}$.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: Induction on $i\in\mathbf N$ gives compatible maps $h_i$, because each construction extends the preceding map. For $x\in P(U)=\bigcup_i P_i(U)$ define $h_U(x)=h_{i,U}(x)$ for any $i$ with $x\in P_i(U)$. Two such choices agree in the larger stage. Addition, graded degree, and the right action are respected by taking a stage containing the finitely many elements involved. Since each $P_i$ is a dg submodule, the equation $d_Nh+(-1)^rhd_P=f$ likewise holds on every element in such a stage.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 13.2(iii) (extension of a homotopy through a semi-free filtration), and section 14.8 (dg categories, with right modules by the opposite category); the calculations here spell out that extension with the conventions of this statement.

proof.text: Thus every degree-$r$ cocycle $f$ is the boundary of the degree-$(r-1)$ map $h$ in the Hom complex. As $r$ was arbitrary, $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(P,N)$ is acyclic. This holds for every objectwise acyclic $N$, which is the stated definition of homotopical projectivity.
